annotationRationale: AA similarity and the squared ratio of corresponding sides determine the smaller area. The Pythagorean theorem supplies the diagonal, and base-height area comparisons transfer the result to ADE.
sourceMethod: Follows the official equal-area comparison and similar-triangle area ratio. Clarifies the official equal-height observation using the equal areas of the triangles on diagonal AC.

review.mathCheck: Independently, AC=5 and the right-triangle projection gives AE=9/5. D's perpendicular distance to AC is 12/5, since triangle ADC has area 6. Thus [ADE]=(1/2)(9/5)(12/5)=54/25, choice E. E lies within AC.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of official solution 15 on page 5. It retains equal areas, AA similarity, and squared scale factors, while explaining the equal heights more fully. The supplied figure agrees with E on AC and BE perpendicular to AC.
review.annotationCheck: cnm_271 and cnm_272 correctly assess AA similarity and area scaling. cnm_174 and cnm_p148 appropriately support the diagonal calculation and equal-height area comparison. No coordinate or additional similarity-model node is needed.
